Indeed, if this were the case, then since ε is fixed in Proposition VI.2 and tn → ∞, we would be able to find n ∈ N such that 2 1−ζ tεα ≤ 1−2 tεn , in which case the conclusions of Lemma V.1 n and Proposition VI.2 would contradict each other. On the other hand, we point out that we do not know whether Theorem A has optimal t-dependence. Firstly, we use Theorem II.4, and we do not know whether this theorem is optimal. Additionally, it seems hard to rule out the existence of different constructions of game graphs that could work better for the purpose of Theorem A.
